text:
Alex: Quick sync — we have multiple reports of spans containing PII (user.email, phone) being exported to third-party exporters. Need a concrete plan for redaction/encryption + key rotation + audit access. @Maya can you triage which exporters are affected?
Maya: On it. Which attributes are we talking about exactly? Any example spans? :thinking:
Alex: Example from prod traces:```span.attributes { 
  "http.user_id": "user-123",
  "user.email": "jane.doe@example.com",
  "user.phone": "+11234567890"
}```
Sam: We should avoid blind deletion. For correlation we need a non-reversible pseudonymization (HMAC with tenant-specific key) so queries still join. KMS for key storage + rotation.
Leah: Agree with pseudonymization, but legal sometimes needs raw values for investigations. Propose a short-term raw retention window (encrypted bucket, strict ACL + audit logs) then purge.
Dmitri: Warning: redaction/pseudonymization can break span sampling / aggregation if fields used as selectors. We need schema-level sensitivity flags so inference/runtime can keep non-sensitive fields intact.
Alex: Proposal draft: 1) Add schema flag: sensitive=true for attributes. 2) Exporter config must support pii_mode=[remove|hash|tokenize], default=hash. 3) Hash uses HMAC-SHA256 with per-tenant key from KMS; keys rotate via envelope encryption every 30 days. 4) Short-term vaulted raw retention: 7d by default, opt-in extended retention requires legal sign-off.
Maya: How do we implement without breaking older exporters? Need backward compatibility plan (old exporters that ignore pii_mode).
Sam: Make agent/collector perform redaction before exporter handshake. Collector will advertise pii_capabilities in the OTLP handshake; if exporter doesn't support, collector enforces default policy (hash). That keeps exporters dumb.
Leah: For audits: add an audit-only endpoint that can rehydrate data for authorized roles (reads only from sealed raw bucket with strict KMS access and audit trail). Access requires multi-party approval.
Dmitri: Also consider telemetry quality: we should preserve a deterministic token for values that appear in span links (traceparent) to keep deduping and joins working. Use keyed hash & expose truncated prefix for UI search.
Alex: Sample config snippet for collector (needs review):```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
exporters:
  file://s3-obs:
processors:
  pii_redactor:
    attributes:
      - key: user.email
        mode: hash
      - key: user.phone
        mode: remove
    hash_key_ref: kms://projects/redwood/keys/telemetry-hmac
```
Maya: One more: telemetry retention + discovery for e-discovery/GDPR data deletion requests. If we hash, we can't delete by original value. Need index mapping to find and remove related raw data if requested.
Sam: For GDPR, hashed values are still personal data in some jurisdictions if reversible or keyed. So policy: raw deletion and audit flow. Hash only for runtime correlation; for erase requests we locate raw in sealed bucket and delete related entries, then rotate keys and re-run redaction job on indexes.
telemetry-bot: [config-checker] pii_redactor schema review queued — ticket #TI-4852.
Leah: Ops/security — ready to sign off on the RFC if we can document: attack surface, KMS rotation cadence, who can request raw access, and retention defaults.
Alex: Thanks — I'll spin this into an RFC with proposed defaults (hash default, 7d raw retention, rotation 30d) and include migration plan for legacy exporters. Can reviewers comment inline once posted?
Maya: +1. I will attach list of affected exporters to the RFC.
Sam: +1 from infra. I'll draft the collector handshake change.
Dmitri: +1 from observability. Will add tests for trace correlation under hash.
telemetry-bot: [scheduler] RFC TI-4852 posted to gh: https://redwood-internal/telemetry/rfcs/4852 — review requested.
Alex: Great — let's aim for implementation in the next sprint.
